scope: offline build only; no flash, no COM, no RF, no probe, no network

superseded_in_part_by.what_changed: phase 1.6 landed the RADIOV10 envelope and the ctx-mandatory command set, so the first reason below no longer holds. The other three still do. This record is left as it was written at 1.5e rather than rewritten, because the image it measures is the 1.5e image; the HEX hash here predates phase 1.6 and no longer corresponds to the tree.

why_not_a_release_candidate: RESOLVED IN 1.6 -- the command set is still RADIOV9 while the protocol contract specifies RADIOV10, and ctx is not yet mandatory on the per-context verbs, which the soak needs once both contexts are bound
dual_sched is compiled in but not on the host-command TX path
the STATS record is not emitted
no hardware gate has been prepared or reviewed, and no guard exists
do_not_flash: nothing here asks the operator to install anything. The image exists to prove the tree links and to measure it.

build.script: tools/build.py, ported from V25: the toolchain is located rather than assumed so the same script runs with the operator's Windows GCC and with a Linux GCC, and the manifest states whether the result is bit-comparable with the lineage
build.incremental: an object is reused only when it is newer than its source and newer than every header this target owns; a full rebuild of this tree over a mounted filesystem does not fit one bounded invocation
build.manifest_paths: input hashes are repository-relative, and SDK inputs are relative to the recorded sdk_root, so the evidence stays meaningful on another machine rather than pinned to one checkout
build.reproducible: two consecutive runs produced the same HEX hash

result.bit_comparability_note: same GCC version, date and branch revision as V17..V25 but a different distribution with a different bundled newlib. Running tools/build.py with the operator's Windows toolchain yields a lineage-identical image; see dual_pan_build_toolchain.json.

toolchain_share_of_that.source: measured on a V25 reproduction, recorded in dual_pan_build_toolchain.json

bss_attribution.sessions: 856 bytes, the two commission_t, against roughly 428 for V25's single session
bss_attribution.ring: 4608 to 5760 bytes, which is exactly 32 slots times 36 bytes of new record fields: the context classification, the parsed header, the configuration generation and the three ACK timestamps with their validity flags
bss_attribution.remainder: about 220 bytes of dual configuration, bindings, the two statistics structures and the scheduler queues

growth_accounted_for.verdict: the growth is where the design says it should be; nothing unexpected appeared in the map

headroom.part: nRF52840, 1 MB flash and 256 KB RAM
headroom.note: the linker placed everything without error at the MBR application offset

verification_method: arm-none-eabi-nm --size-sort -S on both images, comparing the largest BSS objects
